**Always-on live transcription on one CPU core: 31.5× real time · 0.331 J/audio-s · 160 ms · 60 MB INT8. Final: lowest clean WER among timed CPU recognizers at ≥14× (2.63% vs. Zipformer INT8 3.03% panel; 2.34% vs. 2.82% full DEV)**

![Isosyll: Always Listening, Barely Computing. Dev-clean WER vs. energy per audio-second (log) for all 12 timed public CPU speech recognizers and Isosyll final and live on the 730-utterance LibriSpeech DEV panel (400-utt clean split), names colored by single-core throughput](docs/paper/money.png)

**Figure 1.** Isosyll v4.2.0 vs. all 12 timed public CPU speech recognizers on one pinned Zen 2 core: the always-on live stream (160 ms, 60 MB INT8) runs at 31.5× and 0.331 J/audio-s (3.08% dev-clean, 5.08% pooled panel; +0.09 pp vs. Zipformer on unselected DEV); the utterance-end final pass has the lowest measured dev-clean WER among timed CPU recognizers at ≥14× real time (2.63% vs. Zipformer INT8 3.03% on the 400-utt clean split of the 730 panel; 2.34% vs. 2.82% on full DEV) at 14.8× and 0.721 J/audio-s; J/audio-s from the paired full-panel runs (R9 for v4.2.0 final, R8 for live, R6 for Zipformer). [Paper](docs/paper/paper.pdf) · [Release record](docs/ultra/releases/v4.2.0.md).

- **Built for always-on, on-device live transcription.** On one quiet Zen 2 core, **Isosyll live** (160 ms chunks, +LM, 60 MB INT8) runs at **31.5×** real time and **0.331 J/audio-s** (**5.08%** panel, **3.08%** dev-clean, **5.32%** full DEV / **2.84%** full-DEV dev-clean, **328 MB** RAM): **2.2×** the paired throughput of Zipformer INT8 at **57%** of its energy per audio-second (paired R8 full-panel blocks).
- **Lowest clean WER among timed CPU recognizers at ≥14× real time.** The utterance-end final pass (the `isosyll transcribe` default) reaches **2.63%** panel dev-clean vs. Zipformer INT8 **3.03%**, and **2.34%** vs. **2.82%** on full DEV, at **14.8×** real time and **0.721 J/audio-s** (**4.24%** pooled panel, **4.32%** full DEV). On the unselected DEV C-half it is −0.93 [−1.23, −0.66] pp, lower WER vs. Zipformer INT8 and −0.66 [−0.79, −0.55] pp, lower WER vs. v4.1.0 final; it costs **+10.3%** CPU vs. v4.1.0 final (its beam-48 confidence gate **+5.0%**, at its 5% budget, locked by owner choice; paired R9 full-panel blocks). It is not the lowest clean WER of every timed CPU recognizer: larger, slower models (Parakeet, Nemotron 560) score lower on this split at several times the energy.
- **Two small artifacts.** A 60 MB INT8 model per mode (live: v4.1.0 weights, unchanged; final: a new weight average), same architecture and engine; streaming keeps the v4.1.0 commit pass.
- **Bit-exact pure-Rust engine.** No external runtime or BLAS (AVX2, AVX-512 VNNI, ARM NEON, scalar), with identical transcripts across **18** cross-ISA witness runs.

Measured on one pinned Zen 2 core (730-utterance LibriSpeech DEV selection panel; § = 73-clip timing subset, ‡ = shared-host H0 interim). Unselected DEV C-half, v4.1 live vs. Zipformer INT8: +0.09 [−0.12, +0.30] pp, inconclusive. J/audio-s: idle-subtracted core J per audio-second (CPU-domain registers only, not wall power): comparators from the R7 matched campaign (73-clip subset, median of 2–3 core-clean blocks), Isosyll final from the R9 and live from the R8 full-panel blocks under the same protocol. The 0.331 J/audio-s and 57% above are the paired R8 full-panel run. Exploratory DEV-only results. The v4.2.0 final pass meets its registered edit gates; live (unchanged since v4.1.0) was released by owner decision after missing registered edit gates; both were selected on the DEV selection half and checked once on the unselected half (protocol and limits in the [paper](docs/paper/paper.pdf) and [release record](docs/ultra/releases/v4.2.0.md)).
